title: UTPC Code
statementMd:
A UTPC Code is similar to a QR code: it is a square bitmap of white and black pixels that encodes data. Not any bitmap is a valid UTPC Code, though. Valid codes must satisfy the following parity constraint: in any $2\times 2$ contiguous block of pixels, the number of black pixels in the block must be even. In other words, the following $2\times 2$ blocks cannot appear anywhere inside a valid UTPC Code:

```
WB  BW  BB  BB  BW  WB  WW  WW
BB  BB  WB  BW  WW  WW  BW  WB
```

where `W` and `B` represent white and black pixels, respectively.

You are given an $N \times N$ grid with some pixel colors already filled in. Is it possible to complete the rest of the UTPC Code in a way that satisfies the parity constraint?

## Input

First line of input contains a single integer $N$ $(1 \leq N \leq 10)$: the size of the grid. Then follow $N$ lines of exactly $N$ characters each. Each character will be one of `W`, `B`, or `.`, representing a white or black pixel already given at that location in the grid, or a blank spot that you need to fill in, respectively.

## Output

Print `POSSIBLE` if it is possible to fill in all remaining `.` cells with a black or white pixel in a way that satisfies the UTPC parity constraint, and `IMPOSSIBLE` otherwise.

## Note

In the first sample, one valid completion is

```
WWW
BBB
WWW
```

In the second sample, it is impossible to fill in the unknown pixels so that the completed grid satisfies the parity rule.
